strengths: Total revenue: 478.834B in 2026 vs 416.161B in 2025, up 15.1% YoY.
Net income: 132.175B in 2026 vs 112.010B in 2025, up 18.0% YoY.
Gross margin: 48.8% (2026) with Products 39.3% and Services 76.2% contributing to the total margin.
Operating margin: 33.01% in 2026, reflecting strong profitability across product and service segments.
Free cash flow: 136.056B, indicating robust cash generation after sustaining capex.
Cash and liquidity: cash of 36.305B and total assets of 404.548B supporting financial flexibility.
Balance sheet strength: debt down over multi-year period (long-term debt 78.114B in 2026 vs 105.103B in 2023) with a debt-to-equity of 0.6969 and current ratio of 1.0232.
ROE reported as 1.1792 (117.92%), suggesting high efficiency in equity returns within the reported base (as provided in the fundamentals data).
Capital returns: substantial buybacks in 2026 (approx. 85.8B in stock repurchases) and ongoing dividend program, indicating strong capital discipline.
risks: Tariffs and trade measures: tariffs announced since 2025 and potential future actions; penalties can be up to 10% of annual net sales if DMA/antitrust actions prevail.

Supply constraints and input cost pressures: industry-wide shortages in advanced semiconductors, memory and storage; constraints can affect ability to obtain components and raise costs, potentially pressuring margins.

Regulatory and antitrust risk: DMA compliance obligations in the EU and ongoing U.S. antitrust investigations; regulatory actions could necessitate changes to business practices and affect revenue streams.
Cybersecurity and privacy: increasing regulatory focus and potential liabilities around data protection, online safety, and AI-related data practices; could impact product features and costs.
Uncertain tax positions and international taxation: substantial gross unrecognized tax benefits and evolving international tax rules could affect reported tax rates and cash taxes.
Foreign exchange and international operations: currency fluctuations can impact net sales and gross margins; hedging strategies may not offset all exposures.
fundamentals.summary: Apple’s fundamentals show a healthy and improving business. Over 2024–2026, revenue rose from 391.0B to 478.8B (approx. 15% YoY in 2026), while net income grew from 112.0B to 132.2B (about 18% YoY). Gross margin sits at a robust 48.8%, with operating margin at 33.0% and net margin around 27.6%, indicating strong profitability across mix shifts between products and services. Free cash flow reaches about 136B, and cash on hand plus a sizable asset base provide clear liquidity and flexibility; long-term debt declined to ~78B by 2026, and debt-to-equity remains below 0.7, supporting balance-sheet health. The company also maintained strong cash generation in the latest quarter, and multi-year share repurchases alongside growing dividends reflect capital discipline. Management commentary in the 10-K highlights margin drivers from product mix and tariff refunds, while noting ongoing risks from supply constraints, tariffs, regulatory actions (DMA/antitrust), cybersecurity/privacy, and tax uncertainties. The 10-Q corroborates continued solid quarterly growth (9M 2026 net sales 364.4B; nine months YoY growth ~16%), though risks persist from external factors. Overall, the company appears healthy with an improving trajectory, underpinned by strong margins, cash flow, and a diminishing leverage profile, albeit with meaningful regulatory and supply-chain risks to monitor.
